title: A Five-String Banjo
description: Meet the banjo through its round body, short fifth string, and the movements of a picking hand.
cardDescription: Meet the banjo through its round body, short fifth string, and the movements of a picking hand.
focus: A typical five-string banjo has a shorter fifth string used as a repeating drone.
solvingTip: Find the instrument's physical parts before the playing actions.
words: BANJO
String instrument with a round membrane-covered body
DRONE
Repeated supporting tone from a banjo's short fifth string
FIFTH
Position of the banjo string that begins partway along the neck
HEAD
Stretched membrane forming the banjo's vibrating surface
BRIDGE
Small support carrying the banjo strings above its head
FINGER
Part of the picking hand used to sound a string
THUMB

ROLL

NECK

FRET

answerNotes.BANJO: Banjos have different string arrangements; this puzzle focuses on the five-string type.
answerNotes.DRONE: A drone provides a sustained or repeated reference pitch.
answerNotes.FIFTH: The short fifth string distinguishes this banjo from common four-string types.
answerNotes.HEAD: Head names the membrane rather than the tuning end of the neck.
answerNotes.BRIDGE: The bridge transmits string vibration to the membrane.

title: A Mandolin's Paired Strings
description: Explore a small picked instrument through its paired strings, curved body, and tremolo sound.
cardDescription: Explore a small picked instrument through its paired strings, curved body, and tremolo sound.
focus: A common mandolin has eight strings arranged in four pairs, called courses.
solvingTip: The number and string-pair clues help cross the instrument's name.

BRIDGE

NECK

TUNE

PEG

CHORD

answerNotes.MANDOLIN: The common eight-string mandolin uses four paired courses, not eight independent courses.
answerNotes.COURSE: Course refers to a string grouping rather than a lesson in this clue.
answerNotes.TREMOLO: Picking tremolo differs from gently varying the pitch with vibrato.
answerNotes.PLECTRUM: A plectrum is held in the hand rather than attached to the instrument.
answerNotes.EIGHT: Other mandolin-family instruments can have different string arrangements.

title: A Violin Bow in Its Case
description: Look closely at a violin bow through its hair, rosin, grip, and adjustable end fitting.
cardDescription: Look closely at a violin bow through its hair, rosin, grip, and adjustable end fitting.
subtheme: A Violin Bow in Its Case
focus: The bow makes strings vibrate through friction; the instrument's bridge carries that vibration into its body.
solvingTip: Separate parts of the bow from parts of the violin.
words: ROSIN
Resin preparation rubbed on bow hair for grip
FROG
Fitting near a bow's grip that helps hold and tension the hair

SCREW

BOW
Curved-stick tool drawn across a violin's strings
VIOLIN

STICK
Long slender wooden or composite part of the bow
GRIP
Area where the player's hand holds the bow
TIP
End of the bow farthest from the player's hand
STROKE
One drawn movement of the bow across a string
STRING
Taut part of the violin set vibrating by the bow
CASE
Protective container holding the violin and bow
TIGHTEN

LOOSEN
Reduce the tension of the bow hair

answerNotes.ROSIN: Rosin helps the bow hair catch and release the string during a stroke.
answerNotes.FROG: Frog is the bow part, not an animal in this setting.
answerNotes.HORSEHAIR: Some bows use synthetic alternatives instead of horsehair.
answerNotes.SCREW: The screw changes tension by moving the frog along the stick.
answerNotes.BOW: A bow produces vibration through friction rather than direct plucking.

title: The Sound of a Steel Guitar
description: Discover a sliding steel-guitar tone through the bar, strings, pedals, and amplification around the player.
cardDescription: Discover a sliding steel-guitar tone through the bar, strings, pedals, and amplification around the player.
subtheme: The Sound of a Steel Guitar
focus: A steel bar changes the sounding string length; it is different from pressing a string directly to a fret.
solvingTip: Use the short equipment words to cross the instrument terms.
words: STEEL

AMP

PITCH

CABLE

TONE

COUNTRY
Music genre often featuring pedal steel guitar

answerNotes.STEEL: Steel guitar takes its name from the sliding bar, not necessarily the body's material.
answerNotes.SLIDE: Sliding connects pitches continuously instead of stepping between fixed frets.
answerNotes.PEDAL: Pedal steel instruments use mechanisms that alter selected strings' tension.
answerNotes.LAP: Lap steel is played horizontally, unlike a conventional upright guitar posture.
answerNotes.PICKUP: A pickup feeds a signal to amplification rather than making the final audible sound itself.

description: Examine the strings, frame, and foot pedals of a concert harp through straightforward physical clues.
cardDescription: Examine the strings, frame, and foot pedals of a concert harp through straightforward physical clues.
focus: A concert harp's pedals change the pitches available from its strings; the player plucks with the fingers.
solvingTip: Start with the instrument's shape and the parts touched by hands or feet.

answerNotes.HARP: Harp designs vary; the concert pedal harp is one particular type.
answerNotes.COLUMN: The column helps support the frame against string tension.
answerNotes.PEDAL: The usual concert harp has seven pedals, one for each note letter name.
answerNotes.PLUCK: Plucking starts the vibration rather than using a bow.
answerNotes.GLISSANDO: A glissando is a sweeping musical effect rather than a single held note.
